label: Keystone Buyout Underwriting
description: Versioned question and binding policy for a control-buyout underwriting case.

questions.title: Which billing accounts share parent-company relationships?
What percentage of revenue is generated by the largest parent customer across all billing accounts?
Which customer agreements have minimum-volume commitments, and which can be reduced or terminated on short notice?
How much revenue is scheduled/programmatic versus repeat-project versus new/discrete project work?
Which top customers have non-standard pricing, margin or service-level terms?
Which EBITDA adjustments are implemented, supportable and non-recurring?
What is the support for the pricing and utilization initiative add-back?
What is the correct normalized working-capital target?
What portion of unbilled WIP is aged, disputed or missing customer approval?
Which liabilities are debt-like and which are ordinary working-capital items?
Which time-entry, billing, ERP and customer-master systems are still active?
What failed or was delayed in prior integrations and systems migrations?
Who owns the post-close integration program and what is the required cash budget?
How are utilization, rework and project profitability defined across branches?
Which contracts require change-of-control notice or consent?
What is the treatment of the founder-related headquarters lease?
What EBITDA basis will lenders use for covenant calculations?
What are the proposed limits on add-backs, cash netting, acquisition capacity and minimum liquidity?
Which executives and branch leaders require retention arrangements?
What board approvals should be required before acquisitions or major systems cutovers?
